stated_reasons_checked.stairs: Holds. AB02 stairs_1_1: authors start equals the 20 N rise (0 to 10 ms), authors window is about 1.1 s, stance ends about 0.4 s before the window end, and there is no next contact on the plate, so heel-to-heel gives no stride. Minor wording issue: windows are longer than one stance (about 1.1 s versus 0.7 s), so 'one plate contact' is loose.
stated_reasons_checked.side_shuffle: Holds. AB12 side_shuffle_1: authors windows last about 0.95 s with starts 260 to 350 ms away from the nearest 20 N rise and ends 260 to 380 ms from the nearest fall or rise; our contacts are about 0.55 s apart. Not heel-to-heel strides. Authors keys here are cross types (left_left, left_right, ...), identical times on both legs.
stated_reasons_checked.curb_and_cutting: The handoff gives no mechanism, only 'agree poorly'; no wrong reason stated. Data show why: in curb_down_1, curb_up_1 and cutting_1 every authors window lies inside one of our spans (34/34, 22/22, 40/40 overlap) but our speed rule merges continuous walking (0.9 m/s typical) into spans of 8 to 33 s (curb) or 3 to 4 s (cutting) against authors windows of 1.5 to 3.8 s, so starts rarely fall within 250 ms. Cutting_1: 0 of 40 starts within 250 ms.

anomalies_for_the_record: The handoff summary says gait tasks match with 'start and end offset 0 ms for every matched window'. Starts are 0 ms for all 3,819 matched gait windows, but 134 normal_walk matched windows have end offsets of 50 ms to 1.35 s (the authors' window ends differ from our next heel contact). Start claim is right, end claim is an overstatement; the findings text only claims start offsets.
